- Acknowledgement: Redwood will provide an initial email notification within 48 hours of becoming aware of an incident affecting Brightwell data.
- Preliminary report: we propose a preliminary incident report within five business days describing scope, affected data types, and immediate mitigations.
- Root-cause / remediation plan: within 30 calendar days we will provide a full remediation plan or, if investigation requires more time, a status update and estimated completion.
- Subprocessors: we included the current subprocessor registry link in the redline cover and propose a clause that commits Redwood to notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days before onboarding, with emergency exceptions documented.

I attached: Redline_DPA_20261006.pdf and a short internal note for legal review. We are happy to execute via AdobeSign; if Brightwell prefers DocuSign we can accommodate.

1) Legal (Markus) to confirm final wording on cooperation / forensic access.
2) Marissa to confirm procurement cadence and preferred e-sign vendor.
3) I’ll upload the final DPA to AdobeSign and send over the link once legal signs off.

Diego Fernandez

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: DPA execution and breach notification timelines for Brightwell POC

Diego — reviewed the draft. Suggested legal language below and a few clarifying edits (see attached text file). Key recommendations:

1) Notification & reports:
   - Initial notification: we can commit to an acknowledgement of a confirmed incident within 48 hours of detection, which will include a description of the nature of the incident, systems affected, and whether Brightwell data is known to be impacted.
   - Preliminary report: within five (5) business days we will provide a preliminary report outlining likely impact, categories of affected data, and immediate mitigation steps.
   - Follow-up / root cause: we will provide a detailed root-cause analysis and remediation plan within thirty (30) calendar days. If additional time is required we will provide a status update every seven (7) calendar days until complete.

2) Scope / confidentiality of reports:
   - Limit PII in preliminary reports; include only high-level descriptions and TLP marking. Sensitive artifacts (e.g., logs with PII) will be provided under an executed mutual NDA or via secure portal with limited retention.

3) Subprocessor notification:
   - Maintain a published subprocessor registry and notify customers of materially new subprocessors at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding, except where immediate onboarding is required for critical security or continuity reasons; in those cases, we will notify as soon as practicable and document the justification.

4) Cross-border transfers:
   - Where data is transferred outside the EU, rely on EU SCCs (or equivalent) and list of transfer mechanisms to be included in an annex. For US customers, clarify usage of cloud provider locations and encryption-at-rest policies.

5) Cooperation & forensic access:
   - Include a cooperation clause requiring reasonable assistance during an investigation while preserving Redwood’s obligation to protect other customers and its security processes. Limit access to the minimum data necessary and require documented requests and a legal basis for disclosure.

I’ve attached a short suggested clause (Legal_Suggested_Language_20261007.txt). Once you both are comfortable I can redline the DPA and sign off for execution.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Legal_Suggested_Language_20261007.txt (TXT)]
